definitions.explanation: Additional value created through processing, service, or enhancement. Used in business and economics for the extra worth added to a product or service beyond its raw cost.

examples.japanese: {付加価値|ふかかち}の{高|たか}い{商品|しょうひん}を{開発|かいはつ}する。
サービスに{付加価値|ふかかち}を{付|つ}けることが{重要|じゅうよう}だ。
examples.english: It's important to add value to services.

examples.japanese: {地域|ちいき}の{素材|そざい}を{使|つか}って{付加価値|ふかかち}の{高|たか}い{製品|せいひん}を{生|う}み{出|だ}すことが、{地方|ちほう}{経済|けいざい}の{活性化|かっせいか}につながる。
examples.english: Creating high-value-added products using local materials leads to the revitalization of regional economies.

notes:
Compound of {付加|ふか} (addition) + {価値|かち} (value). A key term in business and economics.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {付加価値|ふかかち}の{高|たか}い (high-value-added)
- {付加価値|ふかかち}を{付|つ}ける (to add value)
- {付加価値|ふかかち}を{生|う}む (to generate added value)
- {付加価値|ふかかち}{税|ぜい} (value-added tax, VAT)

USAGE:
{付加価値|ふかかち}{税|ぜい} is the formal term for VAT. In Japan, the equivalent is {消費|しょうひ}{税|ぜい} (consumption tax), though {付加価値|ふかかち}{税|ぜい} is used when discussing tax systems internationally.
